resource.name: City of Calgary-Owned Buildings: Environmental Performance Metrics
resource.description:
This dataset provides environmental performance metrics for City of Calgary-owned buildings, including energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, and water usage. Collected through BenchmarkYYC, Calgary’s building performance benchmarking program, the data supports transparency and accountability in municipal operations. It enables residents, researchers, and policymakers to monitor progress toward climate, energy efficiency, and water conservation goals, fostering informed decision-making and continuous improvement in building sustainability.

Blank cells indicate data points that are unavailable or cannot be calculated.

resource.name: Calgary Existing Buildings - Performance Metrics
resource.description: This dataset summarizes building energy and water reporting information submitted through BenchmarkYYC. Results are grouped by reporting year and property type to support public comparison of building energy and water use, emissions, and estimated energy costs. Data source Year, property type, number of buildings, gross floor area, electricity use, natural gas use, district hot water use, and water use are based on information reported to BenchmarkYYC through ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager. Calculated values Greenhouse gas emissions, energy costs, and related intensity values are calculated by The City of Calgary using local emission factors and cost-estimation assumptions. These calculated values may differ from values shown in ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager. Energy cost estimates Energy cost values are estimates for comparison only. They are not actual utility bills, audited costs, rate forecasts, or site-specific billing amounts. Aggregation Each row represents a group of buildings by year and property type. Sum fields show group totals. Median fields show the middle value within the group. Small groups The summary includes only year/property-type groups with at least 3 submissions. This threshold is based on submissions, not the summed quantity of buildings. Results for small groups should still be interpreted with caution. District hot water Most buildings do not use district hot water. Median district hot water use is calculated from non-zero district hot water values only and is blank where no non-zero values are available. Data quality Results depend on the completeness and accuracy of submitted BenchmarkYYC data. Values should be interpreted as comparative summary information, not as audited building performance statements. Water use reporting Water use reporting is not widely completed by participating organizations in ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager through to BenchmarkYYC, so water-use values should be interpreted as limited and not representative of all participants. Contact For questions about this dataset and BenchmarkYYC, contact energybenchmarking@calgary.ca.

resource.name: Calgary New Buildings - Performance Metrics
resource.description: This dataset provides aggregated information on new building energy code compliance submissions in Calgary. Each row summarizes buildings by year, energy performance classification, and property type, and reports average values for construction value, gross floor area, building height, energy use, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and energy cost metrics prepared for Open Data reporting. The dataset is derived from building performance information submitted to support energy code compliance for new construction projects. Reported performance values reflect proposed building designs and associated reference-building comparisons under the applicable compliance method. These values are modelled or calculated for compliance and reporting purposes and may differ from measured building performance after construction and occupancy. The data is subject to the following considerations: 1. Aggregation and Scope Each row represents an aggregated summary, not an individual building. Property Count shows the number of records included for the combination of year, energy performance classification, and property type. Averages may be influenced by the number, size, and mix of buildings represented in each category. 2. Estimated Construction Value Estimated construction value is based on PMV (Prevailing Market Value) as calculated for Calgary permitting. PMV includes shell, interiors, services, and general requirements, profit, and allowances, including foundations, structure, exterior enclosure, partitions and doors, finishes, fittings and equipment, mechanical, electrical, site requirements, contractor profit, design and pricing allowance, and construction allowance. 3. Energy, Emissions, and Cost Metrics Energy use, GHG emissions, and energy cost metrics are estimated values based on the proposed building design and the reporting assumptions used for compliance and Open Data reporting. Electricity and natural gas costs are based on reporting cost assumptions and may not reflect current site-specific rates, contract pricing, or future utility tariffs. 4. Reference and Proposed Performance Fields labelled “reference” or “vs reference” reflect comparison to the applicable reference building defined by the relevant energy code compliance method. Fields labelled “proposed” reflect the submitted building design. Energy reduction vs reference is reported as a percentage reduction in energy use intensity relative to the applicable reference case. 5. Emissions Factors and Reporting Assumptions Electricity GHG emissions reflect the electricity emissions factors used for reporting and may change over time. Natural gas GHG emissions reflect standard combustion-based reporting factors. Reported emissions and costs should be interpreted as estimate-based reporting values rather than direct measurements. 6. Rounding, Data Quality, and Use Totals and averages may not sum exactly because of rounding. Some combinations may have limited record counts, and the published values should be interpreted with appropriate caution. This dataset is provided “as is” for informational purposes only. The City of Calgary makes no warranties regarding accuracy or completeness and assumes no liability for the use of this data. For questions regarding this dataset, please contact energybenchmarking@calgary.ca.

resource.name: Home Upgrades Program Results
resource.description: This dataset contains building-level records for Calgary homes that completed upgrades through the City of Calgary-funded Home Upgrades Program. Each row represents one building and includes program details, completed upgrade measures, and estimated annual energy, greenhouse gas (GHG), and utility cost savings. Scope and coverage The dataset includes residential projects completed from 2023 through the latest data update. Only completed projects are included. Approved or in-progress projects are excluded and may be added after they are completed. Each row represents one building completion record. How to read the fields Program fields, such as Year, Property Type, Program Phase, and Participant Type, describe the project when it was completed. Upgrade fields are recorded as either 0/1 indicators or reported quantities. A value of 0 means the upgrade was not recorded for that building. “Completed projects” is the number of upgrade measure fields with a value greater than 0 for that building. It is not a count of buildings. Units are included in field names where applicable, such as GJ/yr, tCO₂e/yr, and $/yr. Estimated energy, emissions, and cost savings Energy, GHG, and utility cost values are estimated annual savings compared with a pre-retrofit baseline. They are not measured savings from household utility bills. Actual results may differ because of equipment sizing, installation quality, occupant behaviour, weather, energy prices, and emissions factors. All records in this release are Program Phase 1 and use modeled estimates. If Phase 2 records are added in a future release, their estimates will be based on EnerGuide assessment data. Emissions factors Estimated GHG savings are calculated by applying emissions factors to estimated energy savings. Electricity factors reflect Alberta’s electricity grid and may change over time. Natural gas factors use standard combustion values for program reporting. Utility cost assumptions Estimated utility cost avoidance uses program-level blended electricity and natural gas rates, not each household’s actual bill. Results may differ from current, site-specific, or time-of-use rates. Rounding and data quality Totals may differ slightly from the sum of their components because values are rounded. A blank means the value was not available or not applicable. A zero means no measure or estimated impact was recorded, depending on the field. Negative values may occur if a future modeled result shows a net increase rather than a saving. Privacy and identification The published fields do not contain names, addresses, or other direct personal identifiers. Do not use this dataset to try to identify participating households. Data currency and limitations This dataset is provided for information and reflects the data and assumptions available when it was published. The City of Calgary does not guarantee that the data are complete or error-free. Data and methods may be updated as new information becomes available. Use of the dataset must not be presented as City endorsement of any product, service, contractor, or analysis. Contact For questions about this dataset or the Home Upgrades Program, contact the Program Manager at climateequity@calgary.ca.

resource.name: Green Buildings Priority Stream – Constructed Building Performance
resource.description: This dataset provides project‑level information for completed buildings participating in the City of Calgary’s Green Building Priority Stream (GBPS). Each record represents a single building permit for a project that has reached construction completion and includes key building characteristics such as entry pathway, floor area, construction value (where disclosed), and modelled energy, greenhouse gas (GHG), and energy cost performance based on documentation submitted at the building permit stage. The dataset includes residential and non‑residential buildings completed between 2022 and the current date, covering multiple performance pathways, including NECB‑based compliance, Net Zero Ready Homes, Net Zero Homes, and Zero Carbon Buildings. Projects that are currently under development or permitted but not yet constructed are not included. As a result, the dataset represents a subset of total GBPS participation and does not capture the full pipeline of projects enrolled in the program. All energy, emissions, and cost values reflect proposed or modelled design performance at the time of permit and may differ from measured operational outcomes once buildings are occupied. The dataset is intended to support program reporting, research, and high‑level policy evaluation, rather than project‑specific compliance verification. The data is subject to the following considerations: 1. Emissions Factors Electricity emissions factors reflect Alberta’s grid mix and may change over time. The natural gas emissions factor (0.054 tCO₂e/GJ) represents a standard combustion value. 2. Energy Costs Energy costs are based on estimated blended electricity and natural gas rates anchored to 2025 values and indexed across other years using a constant annual escalation rate. These estimates may not reflect current or site‑specific utility tariffs. 3. Solar PV Solar electricity is valued at an energy‑only rate and does not offset the full blended electricity rate. No premium export programs or solar club rates are assumed. 4. Modelled Performance Energy, emissions, and cost results are derived from energy modelling and may differ from actual building performance due to operational, weather, and occupant factors. 5. Reference Buildings Percentage savings are calculated relative to a code‑minimum reference building (NBC‑AE 2023 or NECB 2020) and represent estimated, not guaranteed, performance. 6. Data Completeness, Currency, and Use Construction value and other project attributes are self‑reported at the time of permit submission and may be incomplete or withheld for some projects. This dataset is provided “as is” and reflects information available at the time of publication. Data and assumptions may be updated periodically as additional completed projects become available or methodologies are refined. For questions regarding this dataset or the Green Building Priority Stream, please contact greenbuildings@calgary.ca
